name: Box Jump
description: The box jump is a foundational plyometric exercise in which the athlete jumps from the floor onto an elevated box or platform, training explosive lower body power through rapid force production in the quadriceps, glutes, and calves. The landing should be controlled and soft — absorbing the impact through the entire lower limb — to protect the joints and train the deceleration pattern. Box jumps are widely used in sport conditioning, athletic development, and high-intensity interval training.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a sturdy box or platform at a comfortable height (begin at 30–50 cm). Feet shoulder-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a sturdy, non-slip plyo box. Begin with a height that allows full foot landing on the box. Never use a surface that can tip or slip.
steps: Step 1: Stand facing the box, feet shoulder-width apart.
Step 2: Dip into a quarter squat, swinging the arms back.
Step 3: Explosively extend the hips, knees, and ankles while driving the arms forward and upward.
Step 4: Bring the knees toward the chest to clear the height, landing softly on the box with both feet flat — hips slightly hinged, knees over toes.
Step 5: Stand to full extension on the box, then step (or jump) down and reset.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale sharply at takeoff. Inhale on the descent or reset phase.
common_mistakes: Landing with straight legs and stiff joints — this increases impact forces significantly
Landing only on the toes without full foot contact
Jumping down rather than stepping down (increases eccentric load unnecessarily)
safety_considerations: Step down rather than jump down unless specifically training depth jumps.
Never jump onto an unstable surface.
Shin scrapes are common when failing a rep — be prepared to bail forward.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full takeoff extension. Land in a controlled partial squat position on the box.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Maximum explosive effort on each jump. Rest fully between sets — plyometrics require high CNS output per rep.
coaching_cues: Hips back and down in the dip — then explode up
